observations: Every fixture resumes a copy of the original VEX state immediately before 0x80011da8. The original preflight independently reaches its first op-5 boundary with 3331 modeled op-6 and op-8 calls in the pinned order.

The main call 0x80013aa8 uses the selected physical block and current payload pointer. On modeled result 0 the original caller invokes the marker and advances the physical block. The same logical block, file cursor and complete source hash are observed on the retry. The successful path advances the logical block, and the next card read supplies the next original chunk.

The original marker calls FcuMediaUpdateBlockStatus and issues op 7 with synthetic request bytes +4=0 and +5=0xf0 for this handle type. In the first-marker-error fixture status 7 suppresses the second op-7 request. The original caller advances to the next candidate with either native marker return.

With status byte +5 set to zero by the spare model at block 1, original FcuMediaGetBlockStatus and the bad-block predicate skip that candidate. The next program attempt uses block 2 for logical block 1.

With the first aggregate program failing and blocks 1 through 639 supplied as bad, native protection checks reject candidates 640 through 1023. The original exhausted-candidate path returns 1 without a second aggregate program. A separate fixture models callback return 0 when the caller still requests another 128 KiB. The original failure branch returns 1 after one aggregate success. Ordinary section completion uses the counters in the caller and can proceed without calling the read callback again.

In the all-success aggregate fixture the original main loop consumes 135 original 128 KiB payload chunks, 10 in section 1 and 125 in section 2. The continuation has 134 successful card callbacks after the first chunk carried from preflight. Compared with the corresponding package chunks, the caller changed 281 bytes before programming block 0 and 512 bytes before programming block 10. The other 133 source chunks matched byte-for-byte. Replay stops before a separate direct op-5 request for 4 sectors starting at sector 0xa00, with no spare pointer. Its caller continuation and any terminal success are outside this fixture.

Section2 first header is retained in scratch and the main source first512 bytes are filled FF. At section end original code initializes scratch[+0x58,+0xd8) to FF and writes bounded physical cursor135 at+0x54. The all-success map needs no conditional B/X/x bitmap corrections. Copying this mutated512-byte header into2048 FF-initialized bytes reproduces the later direct request SHA exactly. Other map-dependent header corrections are static-only.

comparison.scope: Pinned K-3 Mark III ARM evidence separately checks update wrapper, input release and completion signaling. This Q7 MIPS replay covers NAND candidate selection and recovery plus a later request boundary. The comparison does not establish shared operations or terminal status values.

limits: The aggregate program model supplies outcome and failure-map effects. The original helper's byte compare was checked separately in eight one- or two-sector fixtures in analysis/loader-storage.json.

The synthetic geometry, installed header, spare contents and return statuses are controlled inputs. The caller and the marked/bad/protected block tests run original instructions. Alternate section policies and physical write protection are outside these fixtures.

The callback failure is a fixture return at the read interface. FileX errors, EOF and short reads are outside this replay. The all-success aggregate case stops before later direct op 5. Terminal success and a live camera update remain outside scope.
